# Continual-ARC observation: periodic stripe completion

Observed recurring task rule (supported by four demos and one solved test): an input grid contains a sparse/incomplete sequence of stripe colors. Extend the stripe sequence periodically to fill the whole grid, preserving the orientation indicated by the marks.

- Horizontal stripe case: each row is a stripe; infer a shortest consistent period of row colors from the solid-color rows and repeat vertically. Examples: demo 1 output row sequence `3,7,3,3,8` repeated (period 5); demo 2 `4,5,4,3,7,2,4` repeated (period 7); demo 3 `9,4,2` repeated (period 3).
- Diagonal stripe case: colors are constant on NW-SE diagonals (`d = column - row`). Infer the repeating sequence of colors across diagonal offsets from the sparse diagonal marks, then fill every cell according to `d` modulo the period. Demo 4 has period 4, residues `d mod 4 -> [8,5,4,1]`.
- Solved test task-63b68e91: diagonal period 5, residues `d mod 5 -> [1,3,5,6,9]`; output cell is `sequence[(c-r) mod 5]`. The submitted output was confirmed correct.

Practical solving: inspect the geometry of same-color marks to identify whether the stripes run horizontally or diagonally; read off known stripe-color order by row or diagonal offset; find the smallest period consistent with all observations (including wraparound); tile the entire grid. Avoid requesting demos unless stripe direction/period is genuinely ambiguous, since requests cost points.

This task has a uniform field, a pair of same-color boundary segments on opposite edges, and sparse marks in one panel. The edge segments have corresponding positions/local row or column indices despite being offset.

3. In the corresponding row/column of the opposite panel (same local index along the boundary segments), fill the full interior span between the boundaries with the mark's original color.
4. Preserve walls and all unrelated background cells. When multiple marks share a row, apply their rays; corresponding opposite rows are fully filled.

Orientation examples: Demo 2 has a right wall and seeds in the right-side panel, so rays run leftward from each seed to it; corresponding rows in the left panel fill fully. Test case has a left wall and seeds in the left-side panel, so rays run rightward from the left wall to each seed; corresponding rows in the right panel fill fully. Demo 1 similarly shows paired offset horizontal walls and vertical rays. Correct test outputs had original color 5 rays from left wall through each 5 mark, marks converted to 4, and full 5 rows in opposite panel for matched indices.
